# dataset.fmri_dataset.FmriDataset { #fmrimod.dataset.fmri_dataset.FmriDataset }

```python
FmriDataset(data_source, event_table=None, censor=None)
```

fMRI dataset combining time-series data with experimental events.

This is the primary concrete implementation of `DatasetProtocol`.
It wraps any adapter that satisfies the protocol together with an event
table describing the experimental design.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                   | Description                                                                                                                                         | Default    |
|-------------|----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| data_source | DatasetProtocol                        | Object providing ``get_data(run)``, ``get_mask()``, etc. Typically a `NumpyAdapter`.                               | _required_ |
| event_table | pd.DataFrame                           | Table of experimental events with at least ``onset`` and ``block`` (or ``run``) columns.  Additional columns are event variables.                   | `None`     |
| censor      | NDArray\[np.bool_\] or list of NDArray | Boolean censoring vector(s).  ``True`` marks volumes to exclude. Can be a single array covering all runs concatenated, or a list of per-run arrays. | `None`     |

## Attributes

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `blocklens` | Alias for per-run lengths during the consolidation migration. |
| `censor` | Per-run boolean censor vectors, or *None*. |
| `event_table` | The event table, or *None* if not set. |
| `n_timepoints` | Total number of timepoints across all runs. |
| `run_lengths` | Number of timepoints per run. |
| `sampling_frame` | Convenience alias for ``get_sampling_frame()``. |
| `storage_backend` | Underlying storage backend when the source is backend-backed. |

## Methods

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [get_all_data](#fmrimod.dataset.fmri_dataset.FmriDataset.get_all_data) | Return all runs vertically concatenated as ``(total_time, voxels)``. |
| [get_censor](#fmrimod.dataset.fmri_dataset.FmriDataset.get_censor) | Return the censor vector for a single run, or *None*. |
| [get_data](#fmrimod.dataset.fmri_dataset.FmriDataset.get_data) | Return data by matrix slice or, temporarily, by run. |
| [get_data_matrix](#fmrimod.dataset.fmri_dataset.FmriDataset.get_data_matrix) | Return all data as a ``timepoints x voxels`` matrix. |
| [get_dims](#fmrimod.dataset.fmri_dataset.FmriDataset.get_dims) | Return backend dimensions when available. |
| [get_mask](#fmrimod.dataset.fmri_dataset.FmriDataset.get_mask) | Return the spatial mask. |
| [get_run_data](#fmrimod.dataset.fmri_dataset.FmriDataset.get_run_data) | Return ``(time, voxels)`` data matrix for one run. |
| [get_sampling_frame](#fmrimod.dataset.fmri_dataset.FmriDataset.get_sampling_frame) | Return the `SamplingFrame`. |
| [with_event_table](#fmrimod.dataset.fmri_dataset.FmriDataset.with_event_table) | Return this dataset with a replacement event table. |

### get_all_data { #fmrimod.dataset.fmri_dataset.FmriDataset.get_all_data }

```python
get_all_data()
```

Return all runs vertically concatenated as ``(total_time, voxels)``.

### get_censor { #fmrimod.dataset.fmri_dataset.FmriDataset.get_censor }

```python
get_censor(run)
```

Return the censor vector for a single run, or *None*.

### get_data { #fmrimod.dataset.fmri_dataset.FmriDataset.get_data }

```python
get_data(run=None, *, rows=None, cols=None)
```

Return data by matrix slice or, temporarily, by run.

The canonical consolidation contract is matrix-oriented
``rows``/``cols`` access. Positional run access is retained during the
migration for existing callers; new code should use
`get_run_data`.

### get_data_matrix { #fmrimod.dataset.fmri_dataset.FmriDataset.get_data_matrix }

```python
get_data_matrix(rows=None, cols=None)
```

Return all data as a ``timepoints x voxels`` matrix.
